obligation: Client notice of a lost key or exposed code
trigger: A client key or card is lost or stolen, or a client code may have been seen by anyone not authorized (including any takeover of the patrol app, email, or code storage)
notify: Each affected client's site contact, by phone, then in writing

obligation: Client notice of other security incidents
trigger: Any other security incident affecting a client's information (reports, post orders, video)
notify: Each affected client's site contact, in writing

trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic personal information) of Florida residents. Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination. 15 more days only if good cause for delay is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a)). The deemed-compliance path in 501.171(4)(g) is not available (no federal functional regulator)
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email, with the date of the breach, the information involved, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - reports hold driver license or ID numbers for about 90 people and injury notes for about 15

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with a synopsis, the count, services offered, a copy of the notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - records hold personal information on about 105 individuals

trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the owner reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination sent to the department within 30 days after the determination; kept at least 5 years
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only if the no-harm path is used (counsel decides)

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Individual notice delayed for the period in the agency's written request
notify: Hold notices; keep the written request

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: No - fewer than 1,000 individuals in all records

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the owner (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the business has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
notify: The owner, who then gives the required notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - patrol app vendor (and its AI model provider) and the email and file provider

trigger: Affected people who live outside Florida (rare; mostly visitors and contractors named in reports)
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of everyone named in affected reports

obligation: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: claim against the liability insurance
trigger: A client or other party makes a claim against the commercial general liability policy (for example a loss after a code exposure)
deadline: The statute sets no deadline; notify promptly and in writing
notify: Division of Licensing, Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a claim is made

obligation: Records to the department on request
trigger: The department requests records during an investigation, including one that follows an incident
deadline: Immediately on request unless the department grants an extension
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - keep 2 years of records recoverable even after ransomware

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
As soon as practicable (voluntary; supports the OFAC mitigating factor)
notify: FBI IC3 online report or field office; CISA

trigger: Incident that may lead to a third-party claim
deadline: Per the policy notice clause (owner to read it by 2026-09-30)
notify: Insurance agent and carrier claims line
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - whether the policy covers any data incident cost is unconfirmed; ask the agent before hiring outside help

trigger: Breach of unsecured protected health information
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a covered entity or business associate (P03 section 1.1); injury notes are personal information under Fla. Stat. 501.171 instead

deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Organizational incident handlers; CSO, SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official; FBI CJIS ISO
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business has no access to criminal justice information and POL-01 9.6 forbids accepting it

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (proposed)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as drafted it would not reach a small private patrol (P03 section 1.1)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Covered equipment or services found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Covered article found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
